items.evidence: pointers are basically just variables that hold memory addresses
items.note: The student correctly defines a pointer as a variable storing a memory address.

items.evidence: you use the ampersand to get the address of something
items.note: The student correctly explains that the ampersand retrieves the memory location.

items.evidence: then the star to dereference it
items.note: The student correctly mentions using the star operator to dereference the pointer.

items.evidence: when you make a pointer, it automatically allocates memory for whatever type it is
items.note: The student holds the misconception that declaring a pointer automatically allocates memory.

items.evidence: pointer arithmetic just adds one byte to the address every time you do plus plus
items.note: The student states the misconception that pointer arithmetic always adds a fixed one byte.
The student did not mention NULL pointers at all.
The student did not explain pass-by-reference behavior in function arguments.

target_reason: Believing that declaring a pointer automatically allocates memory can lead to severe memory bugs and segmentation faults.
target_focus: what happens to the memory when you create a pointer without allocating
